::: {.why}
Trading fast costs impact and trading slow costs risk, and the whole content of execution theory is that the balance between them depends on a preference you have to state rather than estimate.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the Almgren-Chriss objective and identify which term is a cost and which is a risk preference.
- Say what happens to the optimal schedule as risk aversion goes to zero and to infinity.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Read the Almgren and Chriss problem setup and the derivation of the optimal trajectory as far as the closed form for linear impact. The objective is expected cost plus a risk aversion times the variance of cost, and the solution is an exponentially shaped schedule whose curvature is set by that aversion.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Explore the two limits: with zero risk aversion the optimal schedule is a straight line, which is TWAP, and with infinite aversion it is an immediate trade. Implement the closed form and plot schedules across a range of aversions to see the family.
:::
:::
